name: Universidad de Deusto
summary: Private university in Bilbao and San Sebastián; its business degree, alone or with International Relations, can be taken 100% in English.

ib.text: Maths in both years of your Diploma, a strong first-year record, and a B2 English certificate from an external exam (First Certificate, Linguaskill, APTIS) for the business degrees.

programmes.name: Business Management and Administration (BMA)
programmes.about: Planning, managing and running business projects across every area of a company, which you can choose to study 100% in English, with the option of a semester abroad.
programmes.overview: The programme covers how a company works across its departments: finance, marketing plans, strategic business planning, people management, and the legal, economic and social factors that shape a firm. Recent content brings in digital transformation, sustainability and data analysis. Classes mix theory with case studies, oral presentations, debates, management simulators and company visits, with managers bringing real problems into the classroom, and compulsory university-managed internships. You can add a complement in digital business intelligence, international management skills, or innovation and entrepreneurship, depending on campus. Graduates take roles across a wide range of sectors and organisations.
programmes.ib: Choose the 100%-English path. Maths in both Diploma years; external B2 English certificate to enter and C1 before you graduate.

needs.note: Maths must be taken in both years of the Diploma.

programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your school record (Deusto asks Spanish applicants for a 7/10 average) and an interview; 450 places shared by all BMA programmes.

programmes.name: BMA + International Relations
programmes.about: Two degrees in five years combining business administration with international relations; at the Bilbao campus both are taught entirely in English.
programmes.overview: Business administration is combined with international relations, so you study how companies are managed alongside the economic, political and cultural forces that link states and firms worldwide. You learn to read business data and the international situation together, to build strategies that account for the environment, and to manage teams and projects in public and private organisations. Teaching mixes case studies, debates, simulations, company visits and speakers from industry, with a compulsory period abroad and compulsory internships arranged by the university. Graduates work in international management in companies and public bodies.
programmes.ib: Taught fully in English at Bilbao only. Maths in both Diploma years; external B2 English certificate required.

needs.note: Maths must be taken in both years of the Diploma.

programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your school record (Deusto asks Spanish applicants for a 7/10 average) and an interview.

separateFrom.name: Business Management and Administration (BMA)
separateFrom.reason: A five-year double degree with International Relations: a second degree, a higher fee, and English-taught only in Bilbao.

notes: The 2027–2028 application window is short: 2 to 30 November 2026, with a €30 application fee.
Your IB English may not be enough: Deusto asks for an external B2 certificate such as First Certificate, Linguaskill or APTIS.
Other degrees, such as Data Science and AI or Biomedical Engineering, are bilingual Spanish–English rather than fully English.
